correctness.rationale: Multivariate Gaussian moments factor into pair-edge exponentials; partition Möbius inversion yields a connected simple-graph sum. Only trees contribute at order 2r-2. Coupling to the globally bounded smooth cutoff diffusion changes any fixed joint moment by an exponentially small amount in inverse squared noise, preserving every Taylor coefficient. Independent Brownian observations leave conditional cumulants unchanged. The 107 exact checks independently match moment inversion to tree weights; they are supporting finite tests.

Earlier finite-recursion literature lacks this specific boundary proof. Classical connected-graph cumulant formulas cover a proof ingredient but not, on reviewed evidence, the complete smooth globally bounded-coefficient filtering sharpness assertion. residual_risks: Classical lognormal cumulant connected-graph formulas may already implicitly imply the unrestricted-coefficient part.

value.rationale: The recent filtering finite-tower theorem leaves a precise all-rank boundary k=2r-2. The constructed bounded smooth diffusion simultaneously attains that boundary at all ranks and all covariance tensor entries, providing an explicit structural obstruction to universally discarding the top-rank terms. The weighted spanning-tree invariant quantifies this obstruction across arbitrary dimensions and orders. The result does not claim optimal numerical recursion or prove any previously stated open problem on minimal ODE dimensions.
